# Liner

> Liner is an open-source e-ink frame that hangs one track from 320kbps.club at a time, twice a day: the cover and its liner notes on a museum label, laid over a map of where the artist comes from. It is a LesWWW project by Florent Bertiaux (Lille, France), released under the MIT License.

## Facts

- What: a picture frame with a colour e-ink panel that shows one music track at a time, like a work in a museum.
- When: a new track at 7:00 and 19:00, or on request from a password-protected control room on liner.leswww.com.
- Music: tracks and albums from 320kbps.club, a hand-curated music discovery site run by Florent Bertiaux.
- Map: the artist's place of birth or formation (MusicBrainz "begin-area", checked against the 320kbps.club feed), drawn as a duotone map from Natural Earth outlines; cities are geocoded with OpenStreetMap Nominatim.
- Colours: the duotone follows the cover's dominant ink (blue, red, green, yellow, or black and white).
- Hardware: Raspberry Pi Zero 2 W; Pimoroni Inky Impression 7.3" Spectra 6 (800 × 480 pixels, six inks: black, white, yellow, red, blue, green); a photo frame with a mat.
- Software: Python and Pillow on the Pi (layout, dithering, display); Next.js on Vercel (control room, map rendering with sharp, Vercel Blob storage).
- Rendering: text is never antialiased; only the cover is dithered (Floyd-Steinberg) towards the colours the panel actually shows.
- Licence: MIT. Source code: https://github.com/kxrz/leswww-liner

## People and organisations

- Florent Bertiaux: creative, curator and geek. Designed Liner, curates 320kbps.club, runs LesWWW.
- LesWWW: Florent Bertiaux's creative technology studio in Lille, France. https://www.leswww.com
- 320kbps.club: hand-curated music discovery, one track at a time. https://www.320kbps.club
